key_insight: Richer database context improved LLM-generated type 2 diabetes phenotyping SQL executability and recall, but real-world precision remained limited.
clinical_relevance: Context-rich prompts may support EHR cohort identification for research, but generated phenotypes require local validation before use.
method: Eight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL with progressively richer database prompts.
Evaluated synthetic and UNC Health EHR datasets using the OMOP data model.
Compared outputs with the eMERGE reference phenotype using executability, F1, PPV, and recall.
evidence_signal: Detailed codebooks raised UNC SQL executability from 0% with limited context to 100%, while highest-context F1 ranged from 0.57–0.68 versus 0.54 for a diagnosis-code baseline.
watch_item: Performance did not transfer reliably: the top synthetic performer dropped from F1=0.99 to 0.64 on UNC EHR, where PPV remained substantially below recall.
paper_title: Richer database context improves LLM-generated EHR phenotyping algorithms
